question: What does the Comfort Club membership include?
html:
What Comfort Club includes

We can't list the Comfort Club benefits yet. None of our current sources describe the plan's visits, discounts, priority scheduling or price. The plan details need to come from the operating team before this page can answer the question.

What we can confirm

  • Memberships are part of the growth plan. The plan expects organic growth of about 10-12% (est.) in the first year from AI answering, booking and memberships (Punctual Pros nationwide plan, Oct 6, 2026).
  • The member base is modelled, not reported. The starting figure assumes members equal about 0.9% of core owner-occupied homes (est.) (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).
  • The market is large. Our nine-county Central PA core has about 965k occupied homes. Between 45% and 64% of units were built before 1980 (Punctual Pros market profile, Sept 24, 2026).

All member figures are planning assumptions, not actual enrollment (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).

Data that would answer this

  • The current Comfort Club terms sheet: what each tier covers for heating, cooling, plumbing and electrical.
  • Price per tier, billing cycle and renewal terms.
  • Actual active member count and renewal rate. These would replace the modelled 6,500.
  • Whether the plan differs between PA sites and the Horvath sites in Ocean and Monmouth counties.

Why fuel type matters here

Plan content may need to vary by home. About 241k core-PA households heat with fuel oil or propane. That share is 44.5% in Perry and 37.6% in Lebanon. Ocean and Monmouth are 78-81% utility gas (Punctual Pros market profile). A tune-up for an oil boiler is a different visit from one for a gas furnace.

Members are the recurring base that makes revenue predictable. Moving from about 0.9% of core homes (est.) toward the planned 32,000 members is one of the cheapest growth levers in the plan.

Next actions

  1. Pull the current Comfort Club terms and pricing from the service team. Publish them on this page.
  2. Report actual active members and renewal rate. Use them to replace the modelled month-zero figure.
  3. Confirm whether PA and NJ sites sell the same plan. Note any differences on the page.
  4. Decide whether oil and propane homes need a separate tier, starting with Perry, Lebanon and Berks.

# What Comfort Club includes

We can't list the Comfort Club benefits yet. None of our current sources describe the plan's visits, discounts, priority scheduling or price. The plan details need to come from the operating team before this page can answer the question.

## What we can confirm

- Memberships are part of the growth plan. The plan expects organic growth of about 10-12% (est.) in the first year from AI answering, booking and memberships (Punctual Pros nationwide plan, Oct 6, 2026).
- The member base is modelled, not reported. The starting figure assumes members equal about 0.9% of core owner-occupied homes (est.) (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).
- The market is large. Our nine-county Central PA core has about 965k occupied homes. Between 45% and 64% of units were built before 1980 (Punctual Pros market profile, Sept 24, 2026).

## Planned member counts (est.)

| 0 | 6,500 | 25 |
| 12 | 11,000 | 32 |
| 24 | 20,000 | 44 |
| 36 | 32,000 | 58 |

All member figures are planning assumptions, not actual enrollment (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).

## Data that would answer this

- The current Comfort Club terms sheet: what each tier covers for heating, cooling, plumbing and electrical.
- Price per tier, billing cycle and renewal terms.
- Actual active member count and renewal rate. These would replace the modelled 6,500.
- Whether the plan differs between PA sites and the Horvath sites in Ocean and Monmouth counties.

## Why fuel type matters here

Plan content may need to vary by home. About 241k core-PA households heat with fuel oil or propane. That share is 44.5% in Perry and 37.6% in Lebanon. Ocean and Monmouth are 78-81% utility gas (Punctual Pros market profile). A tune-up for an oil boiler is a different visit from one for a gas furnace.

Members are the recurring base that makes revenue predictable. Moving from about 0.9% of core homes (est.) toward the planned 32,000 members is one of the cheapest growth levers in the plan.

## Next actions

1. Pull the current Comfort Club terms and pricing from the service team. Publish them on this page.
2. Report actual active members and renewal rate. Use them to replace the modelled month-zero figure.
3. Confirm whether PA and NJ sites sell the same plan. Note any differences on the page.
4. Decide whether oil and propane homes need a separate tier, starting with Perry, Lebanon and Berks.
